mission.title: coredns: Panic in route53 plugin fails to release lock and stops responding.
mission.description: A panic (invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference) in the CoreDNS route53 plugin leaves zMu held, after which CoreDNS stops responding to all queries. This issue affects 8+ users.

steps.title: Identify coredns troubleshoot symptoms
steps.description:
Check for the issue in your coredns deployment:
```bash
kubectl get pods -n coredns -l app.kubernetes.io/name=coredns
kubectl logs -l app.kubernetes.io/name=coredns -n coredns --tail=100 | grep -i error
```
Look for error: `invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference`

steps.title: Review coredns configuration
steps.description:
Inspect the relevant coredns configuration:
```bash
kubectl get all -n coredns -l app.kubernetes.io/name=coredns
kubectl get configmap -n coredns -l app.kubernetes.io/part-of=coredns
```
**What happened**:
We use the `route53` plugin with a basic config 
```
route53 <SOME_INTERNAL_DOMAIN>.:<SOME_HOSTED_ZONE> {
  fallthrough
}
```
This works well for _almost_ all requests.

steps.title: Upgrade CoreDNS to a release containing the route53 lock fix
steps.description:
Root cause: ServeDNS holds zMu.RLock() for the whole duration of zone.Lookup(ctx, state, qname). When a record is a CNAME pointing outside the configured zone, Lookup calls into Upstream.Lookup, which re-enters the plugin chain and can block on real network I/O. Go's sync.RWMutex blocks new RLock() calls once a writer (the zone-refresh goroutine's zMu.Lock()) is waiting, so every subsequent query deadlocks and CoreDNS stops responding.

The fix is upstream in https://github.com/coredns/coredns/pull/8601 (releases zMu before calling zone.Lookup). Upgrade CoreDNS to the first release newer than v1.14.7 that includes that PR:
```bash
kubectl -n coredns set image deployment/coredns coredns=coredns/coredns:<FIXED_VERSION>
kubectl -n coredns rollout status deployment/coredns
```
Until you can upgrade, mitigate by restarting deadlocked pods and avoiding CNAME records in the Route53 hosted zone that point outside the configured zones:
```bash
kubectl -n coredns rollout restart deployment/coredns
```

steps.title: Confirm Panic in route53 plugin fails to release lock and… is resolved
steps.description:
Verify the fix by checking that the original error no longer occurs:
```bash
kubectl logs -l app.kubernetes.io/name=coredns -n coredns --tail=50 --since=5m
kubectl get events -n coredns --sort-by='.lastTimestamp' | tail -10
```
Confirm that `invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference` no longer appears in logs.

resolution.summary: The outage happens because ServeDNS holds zMu.RLock() for the whole duration of zone.Lookup(ctx, state, qname); when a record is a CNAME pointing outside the configured zone, Lookup re-enters the plugin chain via Upstream.Lookup and can block on network I/O while still holding the lock. Once the zone-refresh goroutine queues zMu.Lock(), Go's sync.RWMutex rejects all new RLock() calls, deadlocking every query. The fix (coredns/coredns#8601) releases zMu before calling zone.Lookup, so a slow or re-entrant upstream lookup can no longer wedge the plugin; upgrading to a CoreDNS release containing that change resolves the issue.
codeSnippets:
kubectl -n coredns set image deployment/coredns coredns=coredns/coredns:<FIXED_VERSION>
kubectl -n coredns rollout status deployment/coredns

prerequisites.description: A running Kubernetes cluster with coredns installed or the issue environment reproducible.
